paraphrase: He lives in the way of the cow, taking food without hands; he burns his learning; hides his nature; behaves like a child, a madman or a ghost; and abandons the body as the praṇava.

checks.note: The e-text gives this text as one unnumbered prose section; the ref '1 (conduct)' means that section. The passage matching the paraphrase is in it (the text begins: 'atha turīyātītāvadhūtānāṃ ko'yaṃ mārgasteṣāṃ kā sthitiriti pitāmahobhagavantaṃ pitaramādinārāyaṇaṃ…').

paraphrase: Brahmā asks Ādi-Nārāyaṇa about the path of the avadhūta beyond the fourth; the rare one passes from kuṭīcaka to bahūdaka, haṃsa and paramahaṃsa, and then, abandoning all marks into water, becomes the avadhūta.
